guide.summary: Notion uses standard OAuth 2.0 authorization code for public connections, with refreshable, rotating tokens and no review needed to start. The traps are elsewhere. Installation scope is permanent once chosen, and the portal hides the Authorization URL until you submit for review, so you build that URL yourself. Access is granted per page by each user, not per workspace through named scopes, so your agent only sees pages each user explicitly picked.
auth_alternatives: Internal connections use a static token instead of OAuth, but creating one requires being a workspace owner. This suits a single workspace you control, not end users connecting their own Notion.

reasons_to_bring_own: You want your own connection name and branding, or a Notion Marketplace listing. Listing is managed separately and requires a Notion security review.
You need to control the installation scope (any workspace vs selected workspaces) yourself, since it cannot be changed after creation.
build_or_borrow.verdict: Use Composio managed auth; you do not need your own app yet because Notion requires no review to start OAuth and Composio already offers managed auth for Notion.

prerequisites.text: A Notion account with a development workspace to attach the public connection to.
The final redirect URI(s) for your app, decided before creating the connection.
A decision on installation scope (Any workspace or Selected workspaces) made up front. It is immutable, and Selected workspaces rules out a Marketplace listing later.
A server-side component to hold the client secret, because the token request uses HTTP Basic auth with client ID and secret.

redirect_uri_rules: redirect_uri is required in the token exchange if it was passed in the authorize URL, or if more than one redirect URI is configured. Otherwise it must not be sent.
The authorize URL must include response_type=code and owner=user.
On user cancel, Notion redirects to your redirect URI with error=access_denied, so handle that case.

blockers.text: Notion can restrict a connection's API access. Retrying will not fix it.
blockers.workaround: Contact Notion support to get access restored.

blockers.text: Choosing Selected workspaces as installation scope permanently rules out a Marketplace listing for that connection.
blockers.workaround: Pick Any workspace if you might ever list. Otherwise you will have to create a new connection, and users will need to reauthorize.

app_specific_gotchas.text: The Authorization URL field in the portal stays empty until you submit for review, yet review is not required to use OAuth. Build the URL yourself from the authorize endpoint with response_type=code and owner=user.
There are no named OAuth scopes. Users pick individual pages, and the picker only shows pages they have full access to, so your agent may see far less than the user expects.
Authorization is per user, not workspace-wide. Every teammate who wants the agent to reach their pages must run the OAuth flow themselves.
Refresh tokens rotate. Each refresh returns a new refresh token, and you must persist it or the next refresh will fail.
Rate limits are 180 requests per minute per connection, or 600 on Business and Enterprise. A separate per-workspace limit is also shared across all of that workspace's connections.

steps.title: Decide installation scope before touching the form
steps.detail_md: Pick **Any workspace** unless you are sure this will only ever run in specific workspaces. Installation scope cannot be changed after creation. Choosing **Selected workspaces** rules out a Marketplace listing later, and the only fix is a new connection. For an agent whose users bring their own workspaces, Any workspace is the right call.

steps.title: Prepare redirect URIs and capability choices
steps.detail_md:
Draft the values the create form needs: connection name, development workspace, redirect URI(s), installation scope and capabilities.

Prefer **one** redirect URI per connection if you can. With more than one configured, `redirect_uri` becomes mandatory in the token exchange. If you only configure one and leave it out of the authorize URL, you must also leave it out of the token request.

steps.title: Create the public connection in the Notion Developer portal
steps.detail_md:
Log in and open the developer connections page. The probe confirmed `https://app.notion.com/developers/connections` loads. Create a **public** connection, which is the OAuth 2.0 type. Do not create an internal connection: that type uses a static token, which is wrong for multi-user agents. Internal connections also require being a workspace owner.

Fill in the values from step 2.

steps.title: Copy client ID and client secret into your secrets store
steps.detail_md: Get both values from the connection's **Configuration** tab. Store them server-side only. The secret is used for HTTP Basic auth on the token endpoint.

steps.title: Build the authorize URL yourself
steps.detail_md:
Do not wait for the portal's Authorization URL field. It only fills in after you submit for review, and review is not required to start OAuth.

Construct the URL manually:

`https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize?client_id=...&response_type=code&owner=user&redirect_uri=...`

There is no OIDC or OAuth discovery document on notion.so (both returned 404), so hardcode the endpoints. The probe showed the authorize endpoint redirects to an install-integration page.

If you would rather not run OAuth yourself, Composio lists a managed-auth Notion toolkit. Its config details were not provided, so verify them before relying on it.

steps.title: Implement the callback and code exchange
steps.detail_md:
On the callback:
- Handle `error=access_denied`, which Notion sends when the user cancels.
- Otherwise, POST the code to `https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token` with HTTP Basic auth (client ID and client secret).
- Include `redirect_uri` only under the rules from step 2.

The response contains both an access token and a refresh token. Persist both per user.

steps.title: Implement refresh with rotation
steps.detail_md: Refresh against the same token endpoint using `grant_type=refresh_token`. Each refresh returns a **new** refresh token, so overwrite the stored one atomically. If you keep the old one, the next refresh breaks. Guard against concurrent refreshes for the same user.

steps.title: Run an end-to-end test with your own Notion account
steps.detail_md: Log in and go through the flow. There are no named OAuth scopes: access is granted per page in the page picker. The picker only shows pages you have full access to, so test with pages you own. Confirm the agent can read the pages you picked and nothing else.

steps.title: Add rate-limit handling and a support escalation path
steps.detail_md:
Throttle per connection:
- 600 requests per minute on Business and Enterprise workspaces.
- 180 requests per minute on other plans.

A separate per-workspace limit is shared across all of a workspace's connections, so back off on 429s rather than assuming your quota. If API access is restricted on the connection, retries will not help. Surface a clear error and route it to a human, because Notion support must be contacted.

steps.title: Write onboarding copy for per-user authorization
steps.detail_md:
Tell users plainly that every person must connect individually; authorization is not workspace-wide. Also tell them they must pick the pages the agent can see, and that they can only pick pages they have full access to. Getting this right prevents most "the agent can't see my page" tickets.

At this point the integration is shareable. An unlisted public connection can be used without a Marketplace listing.

steps.title: Optional: create a Marketplace listing and submit for review
steps.detail_md: Only do this if you want discoverability in the Marketplace. Listing details live in the separate **Listings** section, not the OAuth setup. A listing requires a Notion security review. This is impossible if you chose Selected workspaces in step 1. Submitting also populates the portal's Authorization URL field.

steps.title: Optional: wait for Notion's security review
steps.detail_md: Notion owns this step. The provided sources do not state how long the review takes or what it checks, so no timeline is given here. Nothing in the working integration depends on it.

belief_diff.topic: Does letting arbitrary users connect require provider review or verification?
belief_diff.prior_belief: Yes, Notion requires a public integration to go through its review process before any user outside the workspace can install it.
belief_diff.finding: The claims say marketplace submission or review is not required to start OAuth authorization, and that listing requires a security review but is optional, since an unlisted public connection can still be used.

belief_diff.prior_belief: Notion review typically takes about 5 business days.
belief_diff.finding: The claims do not address review turnaround time.

belief_diff.topic: Limits while the app is unapproved
belief_diff.prior_belief: An unapproved public integration can only be installed by workspaces the developer controls, and it is capped at 1 workspace beyond the owner's own.
belief_diff.finding: The claims do not state any installation cap for unapproved public connections; they only describe installation scope as any workspace or selected workspaces.

belief_diff.prior_belief: Notion charges no fee to create or publish an OAuth integration.
belief_diff.finding: The claims do not address fees or pricing for creating or publishing integrations.

belief_diff.topic: Key prerequisites (domain, privacy policy, video, business verification)
belief_diff.prior_belief: Notion requires a public website domain, a privacy policy URL, a company or contact email, and a demo video, but no business verification.
belief_diff.finding: The claims list the create form's required fields as connection name, development workspace, redirect URI(s), installation scope, and capabilities, and do not mention a domain, privacy policy, email, video, or business verification.

belief_diff.prior_belief: Notion requires redirect URIs to use HTTPS and to exactly match one of the URIs registered in the integration settings.
belief_diff.finding: The claims only say redirect_uri is required in the token exchange if it was sent in the authorize URL or more than one URI is configured; they say nothing about HTTPS or exact matching.
